description: Use case: the numbers and formulas that a CBAM calculator needs to estimate the CBAM certificates and the cost of an import into the EU in the definitive period from 2026. The embedded emission of a good is its mass times its specific embedded emission (Regulation (EU) 2023/956, Article 7 and Annex IV); the CBAM obligation is the embedded emission minus the adjustment for the free allocation that EU producers of the same good still receive (Article 31, with the phase-out shares of the EU ETS Directive) and minus the carbon price effectively paid in the country of origin, converted to certificates by the CBAM certificate price (Article 9); the cost is the obligation times the certificate price, one certificate per tonne CO2-eq. The worked example is 1000 tonne of hot metal (pig iron) imported in 2026 with an assumed specific embedded emission of 2 tonne CO2-eq per tonne, an assumed carbon price of 10 EUR per tonne CO2-eq paid in the country of origin and an assumed CBAM certificate price of 80 EUR per tonne CO2-eq; the free allocation adjustment uses the EU ETS benchmark of hot metal for 2021 to 2025, because the CBAM benchmarks per good of the definitive period are set by a separate implementing act. The second worked example is the default model of the page 'CBAM Part Tree Calculator' (src/test/resources/web/html/use_cases/CBAM_tree_calculator_sample.html): 100 tonne of galvanised welded steel tubes (CN 7306) imported from Türkiye in 2026, made of hot-rolled coil and a zinc coating, the coil of BF-BOF crude steel and the crude steel of coke and sintered ore. Each part carries its own inputs per tonne of the part: the direct process emission, the electricity consumption with the grid emission intensity of the country, the transport legs with the transport intensity of the mode, the plant construction emission spread over the lifetime output of the plant and the end of life emission net of the recycling credit. The indirect, transport, capital good and end of life emission of each part are formulas of this file; the roll-up over the part tree (the own emission plus the quantity of each sub-part times its emission, to any depth) needs a sum over the sub-parts, so the specific embedded emission under the rules, the full chain emission and the weighted free allocation benchmark of each part are stored as modelled values, and the shipment chain from these values to the certificates and the cost is reproduced by the calc-validation. Under the rules only the direct emission of a good and of its precursors counts, plus the indirect emission for cement, fertilisers and electricity; the full chain adds the electricity outside the rules, the transport, the capital goods and the end of life. The page also offers the default values per good (with the mark-up of 10 percent in 2026, 20 in 2027 and 30 from 2028, 1 for fertilisers), the route benchmark of a good declared by default value and the presets of the grid emission intensity and the transport intensity; the cost path to 2034 is the same chain with the free allocation share of each year. Not covered by a formula: the floor of the certificates at zero and the cap of the carbon price deduction at the obligation, which need a minimum function, and the annual 50 tonne exemption check, which needs a comparison and is stated as a value only.

triples.name: free allocation share

triples.name: capital good

formulas.name: embedded emission formula
formulas.description: the embedded emission of an import: the mass of the good times its specific embedded emission (Regulation (EU) 2023/956, Annex IV)

formulas.name: free allocation adjustment formula
formulas.description: the embedded emission that is not charged in a year: the mass of the good times the free allocation benchmark of the good times the free allocation share of the year (Article 31)
formulas.expression: "free allocation adjustment" = "mass" * "free allocation benchmark" * "free allocation share"

formulas.name: carbon price deduction formula
formulas.description: the certificates covered by the carbon price paid in the country of origin: the embedded emission times the share of it covered by the foreign carbon price times the carbon price paid there divided by the CBAM certificate price (Article 9)
formulas.expression: "carbon price deduction" = "embedded emission" * "origin carbon price coverage" * "origin country carbon price" / "CBAM certificate price"

formulas.name: CBAM obligation formula
formulas.description: the CBAM certificates to surrender: the embedded emission minus the free allocation adjustment and minus the carbon price deduction
formulas.expression: "CBAM obligation" = "embedded emission" - "free allocation adjustment" - "carbon price deduction"

formulas.name: CBAM cost formula
formulas.description: the cost of the CBAM certificates: one certificate per tonne CO2-eq of the obligation times the CBAM certificate price

formulas.name: specific CBAM cost formula
formulas.description: the CBAM cost per tonne of the imported good

formulas.name: indirect emission formula
formulas.description: the indirect emission of a production step per tonne: its electricity consumption times the grid emission intensity of the country, converted from gram to tonne

formulas.name: transport emission formula
formulas.description: the emission of one transport leg per tonne of the part: the distance times the transport intensity of the mode, converted from gram to tonne

formulas.name: capital good emission formula
formulas.description: the share of the plant construction emission carried by one tonne of output
formulas.expression: "capital good emission" = "plant construction emission" / "plant lifetime output"

formulas.name: end of life emission formula
formulas.description: the net end of life emission per tonne: the disposal emission of the share not recycled minus the recycling credit of the share recycled
formulas.expression: "end of life emission" = "disposal emission" * ( 1 - "recycling rate" ) - "recycling credit" * "recycling rate"

formulas.name: full chain obligation formula
formulas.description: the CBAM certificates if the full chain emission were counted: the mass times the full chain emission minus the same free allocation adjustment and carbon price deduction as under the rules
formulas.expression: "full chain obligation" = "mass" * "full chain emission" - "free allocation adjustment" - "carbon price deduction"

formulas.name: full chain CBAM cost formula
formulas.description: the cost of the CBAM certificates if the full chain emission were counted
formulas.expression: "full chain CBAM cost" = "full chain obligation" * "CBAM certificate price"

sources.name: Regulation (EU) 2023/956
sources.description: Regulation (EU) 2023/956 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism, OJ L 130, 16.5.2023. Article 3 defines the embedded emission and the CBAM certificate, Article 7 and Annex IV the calculation of the embedded emission, Article 9 the deduction of the carbon price paid in the country of origin, Article 21 the price of the certificates and Article 31 the adjustment for the free allocation; Annex I lists the goods: cement, electricity, fertilisers, iron and steel, aluminium and hydrogen.

sources.name: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083
sources.description: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as regards simplifying and strengthening the carbon border adjustment mechanism (Omnibus simplification). Replaces the exemption of 150 EUR per consignment by an annual mass threshold of 50 tonne per importer for iron and steel, aluminium, cement and fertilisers, and sets the certificate price of 2026 as the quarterly average of the EU ETS auction prices.

sources.name: Directive (EU) 2023/959
sources.description: Directive (EU) 2023/959 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 amending Directive 2003/87/EC establishing a system for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Union. Article 10a(1a) phases out the free allocation for the CBAM sectors: the allocation is reduced by 2.5 percent in 2026, 5 in 2027, 10 in 2028, 22.5 in 2029, 48.5 in 2030, 61 in 2031, 73.5 in 2032, 86 in 2033 and ends in 2034.
